description: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE as a STATEMENT, live-verified: not an expression (SELECT EXECUTE IMMEDIATE is a syntax error); at session level the SQL source must be a string literal, $$..$$ literal or variable (a || concatenation is a syntax error) and USING is refused (a non-name argument is a syntax error at its own position); both restrictions lift inside a scripting block where the source may be any expression and USING binds ? placeholders; the statement returns the inner query's result set, empty results included. Converted 1:1 from expressions/ExecuteImmediateExpressionTest (now retired).

steps.sql: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'SELECT 1'
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, v INTEGER)
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10), (2, 20), (3, 30)
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'SELECT SUM(v) FROM t'
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, v INTEGER)
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10), (2, 20), (3, 30)
EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'SELECT v FROM t WHERE id = ?' USING (2)

error.messageContains: syntax error line 1 at position 56 unexpected '2'.
